newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise after August NAPM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds rise after August NAPM.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities prices jumped around on Tuesday before settling moderately higher in afternoon trading.
Pass-throughs rose 2/32 to 8/32 with Treasuries after the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) August index came in close to expectations.
Current-coupon Ginnie Mae 30-years outperformed other pass-throughs early in the afternoon, but traders said low volume may have exaggerated the effect.
"I'm sure there's a little buying going on, but it's been quiet," one trader said.
Late Thursday afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were up 6/32 at 100-05/32, yielding 115 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were up 6/32 at 100-05/32, and FHLMCs were 5/32 higher at 100-05/32.

Friday's August employment report has the spotlight this week, fixed-income analysts said. Economists surveyed on Friday forecast 244,000 new jobs were added last month, along with a 0.3 percent increase in average hourly earnings and a downtick in the unemployment rate.
